title: What Burns Do: Burn Shock, Smoke, Chemicals and Electricity
next: Chapter 23, Lesson 2: Assessing and treating burns: depth, size, cooling and fluids

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already put out the fire, give oxygen, cool, cover, and keep the patient warm. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Why a burn hurts the whole body, and why burn shock comes late
  2. Spot the hidden killers: smoke, CO, chemicals, electricity
  3. Know what the PCP adds in the BC Electrical Contact protocol

Textbook: Chapter 23, PDF pages 1898–1931
slides.say: Welcome back. Today we start Chapter twenty-three: burns. As EMRs, you already put out the fire, give oxygen, cool the burn, cover it, and keep the patient warm. As a PCP, you need more of the why, because a burn can hurt the whole body. In this first lesson we'll see what each kind of burn does inside the body: heat, smoke, carbon monoxide, chemicals, electricity, lightning, and radiation. And we'll see exactly what the PCP adds in the BC Electrical Contact protocol.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。今天开始第二十三章：烧伤。作为 EMR，你们已经会灭火、给氧、冷却创面、覆盖伤口、给病人保暖。作为 PCP，你需要更多地理解「为什么」，因为烧伤会伤及全身。这第一节课，我们看每一种烧伤在身体里造成什么：热力、烟雾、一氧化碳、化学品、电、雷击和辐射。我们还会看清楚，在 BC 的触电（Electrical Contact）流程里，PCP 具体多做什么。

slides.title: Skin: why a burn hits the whole body
slides.body:
Skin is an organ, not just a wrapper

Barrierkeeps germs and chemicals outlost → infection
Sealkeeps water inlost → fluid loss
Thermostatcontrols body heatlost → hypothermia

Skin damage starts above 44°C. Singed nose hair, eyebrows or eyelashes → think airway.
slides.say: Let's start with the skin. It's the largest organ in the body, and it has three big jobs. It's a barrier that keeps germs and chemicals out. It's a seal that keeps water in. And it's a thermostat that controls body heat. When a large area burns, all three fail: infection becomes a risk, fluid leaks out, and the patient gets cold fast. Skin damage starts above forty-four degrees Celsius. One more clue: look closely at the nose hair, eyebrows, and eyelashes. If they're singed, think about the airway.
slides.sayZh: 先从皮肤说起。皮肤是人体最大的器官，有三项大任务：它是屏障，挡住细菌和化学品；它是密封层，把水分留在体内；它是恒温器，调节体温。大面积烧伤时，三样同时失灵：容易感染、体液外漏、病人很快变冷。皮肤温度超过四十四摄氏度就会开始受损。还有一条线索：仔细看鼻毛、眉毛和睫毛，如果被烧焦了，要想到气道。

slides.title: Heat burns: five sources
slides.body:
SourceWhat to know
Flamemost common; often deep; may come with smoke
Scaldlarge area; true depth unclear for 24–48 h
Contactusually shallow, unless the person couldn't pull away
Steamcan burn the airway below the vocal cords
Flashusually minor; look for blast injuries

Abuse red flags: shaped burns; buttocks, genitals, thighs.
slides.say: Heat burns come from five main sources. Flame burns are the most common, often deep, and may come with smoke inhalation. Scalds from hot liquids cover large areas, and their true depth may not show for twenty-four to forty-eight hours. Contact burns are usually shallow, because we pull away, unless the person couldn't, like someone unconscious or drunk. Steam can burn the airway below the vocal cords. Flash burns from explosions are usually minor; the blast injuries matter more. And in children, older adults, or people with disabilities, shaped burns or burns on the buttocks, genitals, or thighs can mean abuse.
slides.sayZh: 热烧伤主要有五个来源。火焰烧伤最常见，往往较深，还可能合并烟雾吸入。热液烫伤面积大，真实深度可能要二十四到四十八小时才看得清。接触烧伤通常较浅，因为人会本能地躲开，除非躲不开，比如昏迷或醉酒的人。蒸汽能烫伤声带以下的气道。爆炸的闪光烧伤通常较轻，更要紧的是爆炸造成的其他伤。对儿童、老人或残障人士，带固定形状的烧伤，或者位于臀部、生殖器、大腿的烧伤，可能意味着虐待。

slides.title: Burn shock comes late
slides.body:
Burn shock starts about 6–8 hours after the burn

  • Fluid evaporates through burned skin (hypovolemic)
  • Fluid leaks out of vessels into tissues (distributive)
  • It affects the whole body, not just the burned area
  • Shock soon after a burn? Look for another injury
slides.say: Burn shock is the big danger in large burns, and it matters more to you now, because you control the fluids. It has two parts. Fluid evaporates out through the damaged skin, and fluid leaks out of the vessels into the tissues, so the whole body swells. But burn shock sets in about six to eight hours after the burn, so you usually won't see it on scene. If your patient is in shock soon after a burn, don't blame the burn. Look for another injury: a fall, a jump from a window, or something that landed on them.
slides.sayZh: 烧伤休克是大面积烧伤的最大危险。现在它对你更重要，因为补液由你掌控。它分两部分：体液从受损皮肤蒸发出去；体液从血管渗进组织，于是全身水肿。但烧伤休克大约在伤后六到八小时才出现，所以现场一般看不到。如果病人烧伤后不久就休克，别怪在烧伤头上，要找别的伤：摔落、跳窗，或者被东西砸到。

slides.title: Heat and smoke in the airway
slides.body:
• Most fire deaths come from smoke, not the burn
  • Hot gas: swelling above the cords; steam can go deeper
  • Red flags: hoarse voice, stridor, soot in mouth or nose, singed hair
  • Swelling can appear during transport; fastest in children
  • Smoke also carries CO and cyanide

BC: high-flow O₂ for suspected inhalation injury or SOB; non-rebreather for smoke inhalation.
slides.say: Now the airway. Most people who die in fires die from the smoke, not the burn. Very hot gas usually injures the airway above the vocal cords, while steam can go deeper. Warning signs are a hoarse voice, stridor, which is a high-pitched sound on breathing in, soot in the mouth or nose, and singed facial hair. Swelling can build slowly, so a patient who talks fine on scene can lose the airway during transport; children swell fastest. In BC, every licence level gives high-flow oxygen for a suspected inhalation injury, with a non-rebreather for smoke inhalation.
slides.sayZh: 再看气道。死于火灾的人，大多死于烟雾，而不是烧伤本身。高温气体通常伤到声带以上的气道，蒸汽能伤得更深。警示征象有：声音嘶哑、喘鸣（吸气时的高调声音）、口鼻里有烟灰、面部毛发烧焦。肿胀可以慢慢加重，现场还能正常说话的病人，可能在转运途中失去气道；儿童肿得最快。在 BC，所有执照级别对疑似吸入性损伤都给高流量氧气，烟雾吸入要用非重复呼吸面罩。

slides.q: A man escaped a kitchen fire. He's talking, but his voice is hoarse, his nose hairs are singed, and there's soot in his mouth. SpO₂ is 99% on room air. What is the best approach?
options: SpO₂ is 99%, so room air is fine for now
High-flow oxygen by non-rebreather, and treat him as an airway risk
Wait for stridor before giving oxygen
Put ice packs on his face to stop the swelling
slides.say: Let's check. A man escaped a kitchen fire. He's talking, but his voice is hoarse, his nose hairs are singed, and there's soot in his mouth. His oxygen saturation is ninety-nine percent on room air. What is the best approach? A, his saturation is ninety-nine percent, so room air is fine for now. B, high-flow oxygen by non-rebreather, and treat him as an airway risk. C, wait for stridor before giving oxygen. D, put ice packs on his face to stop the swelling. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 考考你。一名男子从厨房火灾中逃出来。他能说话，但声音嘶哑，鼻毛烧焦，嘴里有烟灰。不吸氧时血氧饱和度百分之九十九。最好的处理是什么？A 血氧百分之九十九，暂时不用给氧；B 用非重复呼吸面罩给高流量氧，并把他当作气道高危病人；C 等出现喘鸣再给氧；D 在他脸上放冰袋来消肿。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Hoarseness, singed hair, and soot are warning signs of inhalation injury, and the swelling can get worse during transport. BC gives high-flow oxygen for a suspected inhalation injury, by non-rebreather for smoke inhalation. A is wrong because the reading may be falsely normal if carbon monoxide is present. C waits for a late sign. D is wrong because the book says never to put ice on a burn.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。声音嘶哑、毛发烧焦和烟灰都是吸入性损伤的警示征象，肿胀可能在转运途中加重。BC 对疑似吸入性损伤给高流量氧，烟雾吸入用非重复呼吸面罩。A 错在：如果有一氧化碳，血氧读数可能假性正常。C 是在等一个晚期征象。D 错在：书上说烧伤绝不能用冰。

slides.title: Carbon monoxide: the oximeter lies
slides.body:
• CO binds hemoglobin at least 250 times more easily than O₂
  • Normal about 2%; heavy smokers 4–8%; 50% or more can kill
  • SpO₂ often reads normal or high: don't trust it
  • "Cherry red" skin is mostly seen in people who have died
  • Clue: several people in one place with headache or nausea

BC: CO poisoning needs high-flow O₂ by non-rebreather.
slides.say: Carbon monoxide, or CO, comes from incomplete burning. It binds to hemoglobin at least two hundred fifty times more easily than oxygen. Normal levels are about two percent, heavy smokers four to eight percent, and fifty percent or more can kill. Here's the trap: the pulse oximeter often reads normal or even high, so never trust it when CO is possible. Don't wait for cherry-red skin, either; that's mostly seen in people who have died. A strong clue is several people in one place with headache or nausea. BC treats CO with high-flow oxygen by non-rebreather.
slides.sayZh: 一氧化碳（CO）来自不完全燃烧。它和血红蛋白结合的容易程度至少是氧气的二百五十倍。正常人大约百分之二，重度吸烟者百分之四到八，达到百分之五十或以上可以致命。陷阱在于：脉搏血氧仪读数常常正常甚至偏高，所以只要可能有 CO，就绝不能相信它。也别等「樱桃红」皮肤，那多半见于死者。一个很强的线索是：同一地点好几个人都头痛或恶心。BC 对 CO 中毒用非重复呼吸面罩给高流量氧。

slides.title: Chemical burns: get it off
slides.body:
TypeWhat it does
Acidpain right away; damage usually shallower
Alkaliless pain, but eats deeper
  1. Protect yourself; remove the clothing
  2. Brush off dry powder first
  3. Flush with lots of low-pressure water, skin folds too

Bleach + vinegar or ammonia → toxic chlorine gas.
slides.say: A chemical keeps burning as long as it stays on the skin, so the treatment is: get it off. Acids usually hurt right away, and the damage tends to stay shallower. Alkalis, like drain cleaner, oven cleaner, lime, or cement, may hurt less but eat deeper. Protect yourself first. Remove the clothing, which removes most of the chemical. Brush off dry powder, because some powders react with water. Then flush with lots of low-pressure water, including skin folds and between fingers and toes. And remember: bleach mixed with vinegar or ammonia can release toxic chlorine gas.
slides.sayZh: 化学品只要留在皮肤上就会一直烧，所以处理原则就是：把它弄掉。酸通常马上就痛，损伤往往较浅。碱，比如管道疏通剂、烤箱清洁剂、石灰、水泥，可能不太痛，却烧得更深。先保护好自己。脱掉衣服，就能去掉大部分化学品。干粉先刷掉，因为有些粉末遇水会起反应。然后用大量低压水冲洗，皮肤皱褶和指缝、趾缝都要冲到。还要记住：漂白剂和醋或氨水混在一起，会放出有毒的氯气。

slides.title: Electrical injuries: small marks, big damage
slides.body:
• Small entry and exit marks; the damage between them can be deep
  • Main killers: asphyxia and cardiac arrest
  • Hand to hand crosses the heart: 0.1 amp can cause VF
  • AC is worse than DC: spasms lock the hand on
  • Spasms → fractures, shoulder dislocations
  • Damaged muscle → myoglobin → kidney injury
slides.say: Electrical burns fool people. The entry and exit wounds can look small, but current turns into heat along vessels, nerves, and muscle, so the damage between them can be huge. The two main killers are asphyxia, meaning breathing stops, and cardiac arrest. Current from hand to hand crosses the heart, and just one tenth of an amp can cause ventricular fibrillation. Household alternating current is more dangerous than direct current, because muscle spasms can lock the hand onto the source. Spasms can also break bones or dislocate shoulders. And damaged muscle releases myoglobin, which can injure the kidneys.
slides.sayZh: 电烧伤很会骗人。入口和出口伤可能看着很小，但电流沿着血管、神经和肌肉变成热，所以两点之间的损伤可能非常大。两大致死原因是窒息（也就是呼吸停止）和心脏骤停。手到手的电流会穿过心脏，只要零点一安培就能引发室颤。家用交流电比直流电更危险，因为肌肉痉挛会让手「粘」在电源上。痉挛还可能导致骨折或肩关节脱位。受损肌肉会释放肌红蛋白，可能伤害肾脏。

slides.q: A lineman touched a high-voltage line and fell about 4 metres. The power is now confirmed off. He has a small burn on one hand and one on a foot. HR 124, BP 82/50. You are the PCP. What is the best plan?
options: The burns are small, so the low BP must be burn shock
SMR, oxygen, look for other causes of shock, IV, 20 mL/kg up to 2 L
Cool both burns for 30 minutes on scene before moving him
No IV: electrical injuries don't cause fluid problems
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A lineman touched a high-voltage line and fell about four metres. The power is now confirmed off. He has a small burn on one hand and one on a foot. Heart rate one hundred twenty-four, blood pressure eighty-two over fifty. You are the PCP. What is the best plan? A, the burns are small, so the low blood pressure must be burn shock. B, spinal motion restriction, oxygen, look for other causes of shock, an IV, and twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres. C, cool both burns for thirty minutes on scene before moving him. D, no IV, because electrical injuries don't cause fluid problems. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名电力工人碰到高压线，从约四米高处摔下。现在已确认断电。他一只手和一只脚上各有一处小烧伤。心率一百二十四，血压八十二比五十。你是 PCP。最好的方案是什么？A 烧伤很小，所以低血压一定是烧伤休克；B 脊柱活动限制、给氧、寻找其他休克原因、开静脉，按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液；C 在现场先把两处烧伤冷却三十分钟再搬动；D 不开静脉，因为电损伤不会造成液体问题。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The Electrical Contact protocol in the BC exam guidelines says to consider spinal motion restriction and, if the patient is hypotensive, to consider other causes of shock, like bleeding from the fall. As a PCP you obtain vascular access and give twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred. A is wrong: burn shock takes six to eight hours, and small marks can hide deep damage. C breaks the exam's limit of fifteen to twenty minutes of cooling, and BCEHS H eleven, as written, allows only one to two minutes. D is wrong because the protocol includes vascular access and fluids.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 考纲的触电流程要求考虑脊柱活动限制；病人低血压时，要考虑其他休克原因，比如摔落造成的出血。作为 PCP，你开静脉通路，按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液，每五百毫升复评。A 错：烧伤休克要六到八小时才出现，而且小伤痕可能藏着深部损伤。C 违反了考纲冷却十五到二十分钟的上限；BCEHS H11 按原文只允许一到两分钟。D 错，因为这个流程本身就包括静脉通路和补液。

slides.title: Lightning: breathe for them
slides.body:
• Huge direct current for milliseconds: acts like a blast
  • A "cosmic defibrillator": the heart often restarts
  • Breathing may stay stopped → ventilate, or the heart stops again
  • Several victims? Those not breathing come first
  • Safe to touch; storm still active → get everyone inside
  • At least 70% lose consciousness for a while
slides.say: Lightning is a special electrical injury: a huge direct current lasting only milliseconds, so it acts more like a blast. It can even burst eardrums. For the heart, it's like a giant defibrillator. The heart often restarts by itself or after about two minutes of CPR, but breathing may stay stopped, and without ventilation the heart stops again. That's why, with several lightning victims, those who aren't breathing come first, the opposite of usual triage. The victim is safe to touch, but if the storm is still active, get everyone inside. At least seventy percent lose consciousness for a while.
slides.sayZh: 雷击是一种特殊的电损伤：巨大的直流电，只持续几毫秒，所以表现更像爆炸伤，甚至可以震破鼓膜。对心脏来说，它像一台巨型除颤器。心脏常会自己恢复跳动，或在大约两分钟心肺复苏后恢复，但呼吸可能一直停着，不给通气，心脏会再次停跳。所以有多名雷击伤员时，不呼吸的人优先，这和平常的分诊正好相反。伤员可以放心触碰，但如果雷暴还没停，要先让所有人进到室内。至少百分之七十的人会有一段时间失去意识。

slides.title: Radiation: time, distance, shielding
slides.body:
Timeshorten your exposure
Distancea few more steps cut the dose a lot
Shieldingsolid material against gamma rays
  • Exposed patients are rarely a danger; radioactive dust can be
  • Removing clothing removes most contamination
  • Vomiting within 1 hour → severe exposure
slides.say: Radiation burns are rare, but know the basics. An exposed patient is usually not dangerous to you, but after an explosion they may carry radioactive dust, and removing their clothing removes most of it. Protect yourself with time, distance, and shielding: spend little time near the source, step back, because even a few steps cut the dose a lot, and put solid material between you and gamma rays. Vomiting shows how bad the exposure was: within an hour means a severe exposure, and within ten minutes the patient is unlikely to survive.
slides.sayZh: 辐射烧伤少见，但基本知识要有。受过照射的病人一般对你没有危险，但爆炸之后，病人身上可能带着放射性尘埃，脱掉衣服就能去掉大部分。保护自己靠三点：时间、距离、屏蔽。靠近放射源的时间越短越好；往后退，哪怕多退几步，剂量也会大降；在你和伽马射线之间放上实体遮挡。呕吐能提示照射有多重：一小时内呕吐说明是重度照射，十分钟内呕吐的病人很难存活。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the Electrical Contact protocol
slides.body:
BC exam guidelines, Electrical Contact. Safety first: don't approach electrical sources or downed lines until qualified personnel deem the scene safe.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Consider spinal motion restriction
  • Arrest: compressions, follow the guideline
  • Oxygen as required
  • Flush with sterile saline; cool ≤ 15–20 min, incl. decon
  • Note current type and contact time; estimate BSA
  • Analgesia only if no inhalation injury

PCP adds

  • Vascular access (IV)
  • Hypotensive? Consider other causes of shock
  • Bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL

BCEHS H11, as written: cool no longer than 1–2 min, incl. decon (H10 thermal burns: 15 min). High voltage: 5 mL/kg, then 100 mL/h.
slides.say: Here's the Electrical Contact protocol from the BC exam guidelines. It starts with your safety: don't approach electrical sources or downed lines until qualified people say the scene is safe. Every licence level considers spinal motion restriction, starts compressions in arrest, gives oxygen, flushes the burns with sterile saline, and cools no longer than fifteen to twenty minutes, including decontamination. Note the type of current and contact time, estimate the burned area, and give pain relief only if there's no inhalation injury. The PCP adds vascular access. If the patient is hypotensive, consider other causes of shock, and give twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred. BCEHS guideline H eleven differs: as written, cool no longer than one to two minutes, including decontamination, and for high voltage give five millilitres per kilogram, then one hundred an hour.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 考纲里的触电流程。第一条是你自己的安全：在有资质的人员确认现场安全之前，不要靠近电源或掉落的电线。所有执照级别都要：考虑脊柱活动限制；心脏骤停就开始按压；给氧；用无菌生理盐水冲洗烧伤处；冷却不超过十五到二十分钟，洗消时间也算在内。记录电流类型和接触时长，估算烧伤面积；只有在没有吸入性损伤时才给镇痛。PCP 多做的是开静脉通路。病人低血压时，要考虑其他休克原因，并按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液，每五百毫升复评一次。BCEHS 指南 H11 不一样：按原文，冷却不超过一到两分钟，洗消时间也算在内；高压电损伤先给每公斤五毫升，再每小时一百毫升。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Shock soon after a burn → find another cause
  • CO possible → don't trust SpO₂
  • Rigid limb or abdomen after a shock → deep damage; recheck pulses
  • Fluids: reassess every 500 mL
  • Analgesia only without inhalation injury; no Entonox with one
  • Book: monitor electrical patients for 24 h
slides.say: Now the PCP watch-outs from this lesson. A burn patient in shock early has another problem, so look for bleeding or a fall before you blame the burn. Never trust a normal saturation when carbon monoxide is possible. Small electrical marks can hide deep muscle damage; a rigid limb or abdomen is a warning, so recheck distal pulses. When you give fluids, reassess every five hundred millilitres. Give pain relief only if there's no inhalation injury; Entonox is contraindicated with one. And rhythm problems can appear later; the book keeps electrical patients on a cardiac monitor for twenty-four hours.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲这节课 PCP 要注意的事。烧伤病人早期就休克，说明另有问题，先找出血或摔伤，别怪在烧伤上。可能有一氧化碳时，血氧饱和度正常也绝不能信。小小的电击痕迹可能藏着深部肌肉损伤；肢体或腹部变硬是危险信号，要反复检查远端脉搏。补液时，每五百毫升复评一次。只有在没有吸入性损伤时才给镇痛；有吸入性损伤时禁用笑气。心律问题可能稍后才出现，书里让触电病人接心电监护二十四小时。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Smoke inhalation or CO → non-rebreather, high-flow O₂
  • Electrical: cool ≤ 15–20 min, including decon (BCEHS H11: 1–2 min)
  • Flush with sterile saline; analgesia only if no inhalation injury
  • Lightning arrest: BC CPR (adult 30:2; child, 2 rescuers 15:2), pauses < 5 s; adult 30/40-min rule
  • Book's calcium gel and potassium iodide: not on the BC exam drug list
slides.say: Here's where the BC exam guidelines add detail to the book. For smoke inhalation or CO, they specify a non-rebreather with high-flow oxygen. For electrical burns, the exam cools no longer than fifteen to twenty minutes, including decontamination; BCEHS H eleven, as written, says one to two. The exam flushes with sterile saline and gives analgesia only without inhalation injury. For a lightning arrest, the book says don't give up early; the exam still uses its CPR protocol: thirty to two for an adult, fifteen to two for a child with two rescuers, pauses under five seconds, and for adults the thirty- or forty-minute rule. And the book's calcium gel and potassium iodide are not on the BC exam drug list.
slides.sayZh: 这里是 BC 考纲在书本之外补充的细节。烟雾吸入或一氧化碳中毒，考纲明确要用非重复呼吸面罩给高流量氧。电烧伤考纲冷却不超过十五到二十分钟，洗消时间也算在内；BCEHS H11 按原文是一到两分钟。考纲用无菌生理盐水冲洗，只有在没有吸入性损伤时才给镇痛。雷击导致的心脏骤停，书上说不要过早放弃；考纲仍按自己的心肺复苏流程：成人三十比二，儿童双人十五比二，中断少于五秒；成人执行三十或四十分钟的规则。书里的钙凝胶和碘化钾，都不在 BC 考试药物清单上。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Burn shock takes 6–8 hours: early shock means look for another injury
  2. Smoke: hoarse voice, soot, singed hair → high-flow O₂; don't trust SpO₂
  3. Electrical: small marks, deep damage; PCP adds IV, 20 mL/kg up to 2 L

Next: assessing and treating the burn: depth, size, cooling and fluids
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: burn shock takes six to eight hours, so early shock in a burn patient means another injury until proven otherwise. Two: smoke is the real killer. A hoarse voice, soot, and singed hair mean high-flow oxygen and close airway watching, and a normal saturation means nothing when CO is possible. Three: electrical injuries hide deep damage behind small marks. As a PCP you add an IV; if the patient is hypotensive, look for other causes and give twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres. Next lesson: depth, size, cooling, and fluids. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，烧伤休克要六到八小时才出现，所以烧伤病人早期就休克，在排除之前都要当作有别的伤。二，烟雾才是真正的杀手：声音嘶哑、烟灰、毛发烧焦，就要给高流量氧、密切盯住气道；可能有一氧化碳时，血氧正常说明不了什么。三，电损伤在小小的伤痕后面藏着深部损伤。作为 PCP 你多了静脉通路；病人低血压时，先找其他原因，再按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液。下节课讲烧伤深度、面积、冷却和补液。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
